did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a musical heading, “For the director of music. According to Jeduthun,” and is attributed to David. The heading points to the psalm’s connection with musical accompaniment or performance.
Did you know? At the very beginning of the psalm, the soul is portrayed as quietly waiting: “Truly my soul finds rest in God.” According to the verse, salvation comes from God alone.
Did you know? God is described through three images of protection and stability: “my rock,” “my salvation,” and “my fortress.” These images emphasize security and steadfastness in the face of danger.
Did you know? The poet describes his enemies using images of unstable structures: “a leaning wall” and “a tottering fence.” This creates a sense of pressure, instability, and the danger of collapse.

Did you know? The verse contrasts outward speech with inner intent: the enemies’ mouths offer blessing, but their hearts contain curses. The text therefore describes a gap between outward appearance and inner truth.

Did you know? In this verse, the call for the soul to wait for God appears again, but this time He is emphasized as the source of hope: “For my hope comes from him.” The repetition reinforces the idea of relying on Him alone.
Did you know? The psalm expands personal trust into national and communal trust: God is salvation, honor, a strong rock, and a refuge, so all the people are called to trust in Him.
Did you know? The command “Pour out your hearts to him” invites the people to bring their feelings and troubles openly before God. Immediately afterward, God is called “our refuge.”

Did you know? Human beings are described here as “a breath” and “a lie”; on the scales, they weigh even less than a breath. The image emphasizes human transience and the instability of relying on people alone.

Did you know? The conclusion says, “One thing God has spoken; two things I have heard.” After this poetic formulation, two central principles are presented: God’s strength and His unfailing love, along with His rewarding each person according to their deeds.
